هذا المستند يوضح خطوات الفحص 
اليومى لجهاز التنفس الصناعى كما هو موضح عاليه.

هذا 
الجهاز هو جهاز تنفس الغرض منه حماية كاملة للتنفس فى جو ملوث بغازات سامة او فى 
حالة نقص النسبة الحجمية للاكسجين فى الجو المحيط عن %17 حيث يقوم الجهاز بعزل 
الشخص المستخدم تماما عن الجو المحيط به حتى فى اقصى درجات التلوث خطورة على 
الحياة.

وفترة استخدام الجهاز 
تكون حوالى نصف ساعة تزيد او تقل حسب الحالة الصحية للمستخدم ودرجة نشاطة ومجهودة 
العضلى وحالتة النفسية والعصبية وحالات الخوف التى تؤثر على سرعة التنفس ومن الممكن 
ان تقل فترة الاستخدام وتصل الى ربع ساعة فقط.

والجهاز مزود بجهاز 
تحذير صوتى يعمل تلقائيا عند فتح محبس الاسطوانه ثم يتوقف عند الاستخدام.

واذا بدأ الانذار يعمل 
اثناء الاستخدام فان ذلك يكون بمثابة تحذير بانه لابد من الخروج من منطقة التلوث 
الى منطقة الهواء النقى حيث يكون متبقى دقائق قليلة وتنفذ كمية الهواء بالاسطوانة.

والجهاز به صمام تخفيض 
الضغط يعمل على تخفيض ضغط الهواء الذاهب الى بلف التنفس الى 7 بار.

ويكون صمام التنفس فى 
حالة التشغيل العادى على وضع الضغط الموجب ويظهر ذلك بعلامة اللون الابيض على مبين 
الصمام

عندما يتنفس مستخدم 
الجهاز فان ذلك بسبب انخفاض الضغط الموجب الطبيعى لبلف التنفس وذلك يحرك ديفرام 
البلف الذى يدفع عامود التحكم لبلف عدم الراجع فينفتح مسار الهواء فينساب الهواء من 
صمام مخفض الضغط الى قناع الوجه اما عند عملية الزفير فان الديفرام يعود الى وضعة 
الاصلى ويقوم عامود التحكم لبلف عدم الراجع بغلق مسار الهواء مرة اخرى فيخرج هواء 
الزفير الى الجو عن طريق بلفى الزفير فى قناع الوجه

ومع استمرار الاستخدام 
ينخفض ضغط الاسطوانة حتى يصل مؤشر عداد الضغط الى نطاق اللون الاحمر فيقوم جهاز 
الانذار السمعى باصدار صوت تحذيرى للمستخدم بان كمية الهواء على وشك النفاذ.

فى حالة تلف او عد 
فاعلية صمام النفس الاوتوماتيكى يتم التحويل الى وضع التشغيل الاحتياطى ويظهر ذلك 
بعلامة اللون الاحمر على مبين الصمام وهو يقوم بالامداد بتيار هواء مستمر ويتم ضبطة 
على كمية الهواء المطلوبة للتنفس حيث ان الضغط فى الاسطوانة يقل بسرعة نتيجة تيار 
الهواء المستمر وفى هذه الحالة يجب الخروج بسرعة من منطقة
التلوث

Industrial breathing apparatus
SEKUR - AIR NPC 1800
Pirelli group

Issued to:
Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station

sections_en.text: This document explains the steps of the daily inspection of the industrial breathing apparatus as shown above.

This apparatus is a breathing apparatus intended for complete respiratory protection in an atmosphere contaminated with toxic gases, or when the volumetric percentage of oxygen in the surrounding atmosphere falls below 17%, as the apparatus completely isolates the user from the surrounding atmosphere, even in the most dangerously contaminated conditions.

The period of use of the apparatus is about half an hour, more or less depending on the user's health condition, activity level, muscular effort, psychological and nervous condition, and states of fear that affect the breathing rate; the period of use may decrease to only a quarter of an hour.
The apparatus is fitted with an audible warning device that operates automatically when the cylinder valve is opened, then stops during use.

If the alarm starts operating during use, this is a warning that the user must leave the contaminated area for the fresh air area, as only a few minutes remain before the air in the cylinder runs out.
The apparatus has a pressure reducing valve that reduces the pressure of the air going to the breathing valve to 7 bar.
The breathing valve is in normal operation on the positive pressure position, which is shown by the white colour mark on the valve indicator.

When the user of the apparatus breathes, this is due to the drop in the normal positive pressure of the breathing valve, which moves the valve diaphragm that pushes the control shaft of the non-return valve, so the air path opens and air flows from the pressure reducing valve to the face mask. During exhalation, the diaphragm returns to its original position and the control shaft of the non-return valve closes the air path again, and the exhaled air exits to the atmosphere through the two exhalation valves in the face mask.

With continued use, the cylinder pressure drops until the pressure gauge pointer reaches the red colour zone, and the audible alarm device sounds a warning to the user that the air quantity is about to run out.

If the automatic breathing valve is damaged or ineffective, it is switched to the standby operating position, shown by the red colour mark on the valve indicator; it supplies a continuous air stream, adjusted to the air quantity required for breathing, as the pressure in the cylinder drops quickly as a result of the continuous air stream, and in this case the user must leave the contaminated area quickly.

It was reviewed by the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Chemist Ahmed Abdullah.

rows: Check the general cleanliness of the apparatus
Check the rubber parts to make sure there are no twists, cracks, cuts, holes or tears
Check the face mask to make sure there are no fractures, loss of elasticity or loss of any parts
Check that there is no wear on the threaded connection teeth
Check the cleanliness of the breathing valve
Check the breathing tube to make sure there are no cracks or holes, and check the tight connection of the breathing hose
Check the tightness of the connecting nut at the cylinder valve and that the sealing gasket is present
Check the soundness of the high pressure air hose and that the sealing gasket is present in it
Check the soundness of the pressure gauge and that there is no air leakage
Check that the breathing air cylinder is completely full
Face mask fitted with a speech device

Introduction
This document explains the steps of the daily inspection of the industrial breathing apparatus as shown above.
This apparatus is a breathing apparatus intended for complete respiratory protection in an atmosphere contaminated with toxic gases, or when the volumetric percentage of oxygen in the surrounding atmosphere falls below 17%, as the apparatus completely isolates the user from the surrounding atmosphere, even in the most dangerously contaminated conditions.
The period of use of the apparatus is about half an hour, more or less depending on the user's health condition, activity level, muscular effort, psychological and nervous condition, and states of fear that affect the breathing rate; the period of use may decrease to only a quarter of an hour.
The apparatus is fitted with an audible warning device that operates automatically when the cylinder valve is opened, then stops during use.
If the alarm starts operating during use, this is a warning that the user must leave the contaminated area for the fresh air area, as only a few minutes remain before the air in the cylinder runs out.
The apparatus has a pressure reducing valve that reduces the pressure of the air going to the breathing valve to 7 bar.
The breathing valve is in normal operation on the positive pressure position, which is shown by the white colour mark on the valve indicator.
When the user of the apparatus breathes, this is due to the drop in the normal positive pressure of the breathing valve, which moves the valve diaphragm that pushes the control shaft of the non-return valve, so the air path opens and air flows from the pressure reducing valve to the face mask. During exhalation, the diaphragm returns to its original position and the control shaft of the non-return valve closes the air path again, and the exhaled air exits to the atmosphere through the two exhalation valves in the face mask.
With continued use, the cylinder pressure drops until the pressure gauge pointer reaches the red colour zone, and the audible alarm device sounds a warning to the user that the air quantity is about to run out.
If the automatic breathing valve is damaged or ineffective, it is switched to the standby operating position, shown by the red colour mark on the valve indicator; it supplies a continuous air stream, adjusted to the air quantity required for breathing, as the pressure in the cylinder drops quickly as a result of the continuous air stream, and in this case the user must leave the contaminated area quickly.
Technical specifications
300 bar | Maximum operating pressure
450 bar | Cylinder test pressure
30 minutes | Operating period
60 bar | Start of audible warning device operation
7 bar | Pressure reducing valve calibration
10 bar | Safety valve calibration
Every 5 years | Hydrostatic test
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed, Senior Engineer of the Occupational Safety and Health Department, and reviewed by Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Technical Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan, Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector. It was reviewed by the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Chemist Ahmed Abdullah.
Procedures to be carried out
Check the general cleanliness of the apparatus | 1
Check the rubber parts to make sure there are no twists, cracks, cuts, holes or tears | 2
Check the face mask to make sure there are no fractures, loss of elasticity or loss of any parts | 3
Check that there is no wear on the threaded connection teeth | 4
Check the cleanliness of the breathing valve | 5
Check the breathing tube to make sure there are no cracks or holes, and check the tight connection of the breathing hose | 6
Check the tightness of the connecting nut at the cylinder valve and that the sealing gasket is present | 7
Check the soundness of the high pressure air hose and that the sealing gasket is present in it | 8
Check the soundness of the pressure gauge and that there is no air leakage | 9
Check that the breathing air cylinder is completely full | 10
Apparatus components
Breathing cylinder valve | 2 | Breathing cylinder | 1
Breathing tube | 4 | Pressure reducer | 3
High pressure air tube | 6 | Pressure indicator | 5
Breathing valve | 8 | Audible warning device | 7
Fixing belt | 10 | Breathing apparatus holder | 9
Safety valve | 12 | Face mask fitted with a speech device | 11
